caption: The funeral policy paid out. It still wasn't close to what the month actually cost once the whole family arrived to be fed. What did nobody warn you a funeral really costs?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R20 200
p/m salary
Living in Ladysmith
slides.body:
Male, 41
Married, two kids at home
Job: Admin clerk, provincial hospital
Net salary: R20 200 p/m (this month, we buried my father)

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: Didn't move, didn't downgrade. Some months you just can't touch the number that's already tight.

slides.title: Funeral costs
slides.includes: Catering for 150 people, tent and chairs hire, our family's share after the policy payout
slides.body: The policy paid out. It never covers what an actual funeral costs once the whole family shows up to be fed.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Feeding the house, plus relatives who stayed the week
slides.body: Double the normal amount, and I only worked that out while writing this down.

slides.title: Transport & fuel
slides.includes: Fetching family from three towns for the service
slides.body: Everyone needed a lift from somewhere. I was the one with the working car.

slides.title: School fees & aftercare
slides.includes: Both kids, doesn't pause for a death in the family
slides.body: The school doesn't do payment holidays for grief.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid, funeral policy going forward, cellphone & data, stokvel
slides.body: Four ordinary lines that kept running quietly through the worst week of my year.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R20 200. We buried my father and the month still had to add up to zero like any other.

slides.title: I stopped guessing what the month actually cost
slides.body:
I uploaded my statement to Beyond Horizon afterwards, mostly to understand what had happened to the money. The catering bill was the number that shocked me.

No bank login needed.
